neighbours.label: the second mention of a unit or kind noun in a parallel pair: 'N tons of A for each ton of B', 'the type of A and the type of B'
fire: The mill uses fifty gallons of water for each gallon of dye it produces.
Add three spoons of sugar for every spoon of salt in the brine.
The charity raised four pounds for each pound it spent on advertising.
It varies with the type of engine fitted and the type of fuel burned.
Much depends on the kind of school you attend and the kind of teacher you meet.
The farm needs six acres of pasture for each acre of wheat it grows.
We mixed two parts of sand for every part of cement.
The furnace burns five tons of coke for each ton of iron it yields.
quiet: The mill uses fifty gallons of water for each batch of dye it produces.
Add three spoons of sugar for every pinch of salt in the brine.
The charity raised four pounds for each advert it placed in the paper.
It varies with the engine fitted and the fuel burned.
Much depends on the school you attend and the teacher you meet.
The farm needs six acres of pasture for its herd of dairy cows.
We mixed two parts of sand with a bucket of cement.
The furnace burns five tons of coke on every working day.

short: repeated unit noun in a ratio
notes: Probes: 'three tons of coal for each ton' 0.95, 'nine dollars for each dollar' 0.62, 'two cups of water for every cup' 0.53, 'the kind of … and the kind of' 0.65, 'the type of … and the type' 0.49; without the repeat ('for every handful', 'for each hundred', 'the soil … and the plant') 0.04-0.10. 'ten miles … with each mile' did not fire (0.02), so the ratio or parallel frame seems to matter. The card's top examples also include unrelated code tokens (isinstance, _repr) and ' unstable', which this label does not cover.
